en: The Sūtra of the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Rank of Chao San Dafu, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fata, by Imperial Decree.
I take refuge in all Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the All-Knowing Buddhas.
I shall now proclaim this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas.
Should there be gods, humans, vidyādharas, or sages who uphold it...
I take refuge in and make offerings to all Buddhas.
Having mastered the mantras through their reception, recitation, and exposition, one penetrates the characteristics of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*).
If one utters the syllable *Oṃ*, it signifies the meaning of perfection.
If one utters the syllable *na*, it has the meaning of being free from fear;
it is also called the meaning of destroying Māra.
If one utters the syllable *ya*, it has the meaning of breaking bonds.
If one recites the syllable *sa*, it has the meaning of subduing enemies and obstacles.
If one recites the syllable *ni*, it has the meaning of destroying adversaries.
For those who are terrified, they shall be freed from fear through the power of the mantra.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
Oṃ bṛ-kūṭa-ṭi-ve ṭi-ve ṭi-ve ṭi-śve tajje ti-sarva-ha sarva... [The text continues with the remainder of the mantra].
HŪṂ KĀRAṂ CAÑCAṆA-PADMA-HṚT-SAT-NUVA-VĀRA-MARA-TRAYA-VINĀŚAYA VIBHOṬA VIMUKTI.
Oṃ jñāna-hūṃ-kāra-siddhi-bhava-jvala-roma-karotaka-tani svāhā | Kāriṇa puṣṭaye vaṃ ja kāriṇa jamanam |
Hrīḥ śāntam akābhedatattvanabhaḥ-kuṭa-sthas-tavimukta-vinayata-mavinaya-dhāri.
Vinyamāravasini vinyajñe devārupe śrīvinyarāja prajñātājitasattvaḥ.
Haya-sattva-vijñāna-gataṃ paṭumaṃ nirmāṇa-paṭum-arcaye paṭu-nirvāṇa-viśālinīm āgaccha.
Ṛṣvatarālo ’ṅgārupeśo ’ṅgikeśa-nimantre-jarvoḷa-nit-pa-ni-lau-dri-kumāri-viśvarūpiṇi.
Ārya-māri-sūtradhāra-śāstradharācārya-dharmabhāṇaka-śramaṇa-pratyekabuddha-bodhisattva-niyamadhara.
Ānṛśa-garāntarāṇi-taraṇi-tattvājñaptattva-sambhava-padmābha-sad-ṛbhavāyārthaka-vi...
Rāvaṇa-māravara-nivāraṇa-sapratijña-pramarditāgraja-gaṅgāśa-vinayitejārin.
Cacchaka-sambhava-mañjari-jāti-jāta-dhāri-prahana-vinyadhāri-varadhārani-dharani-dhati-namavinya.
*Parakramacakṣuḥ-prajñācakṣur-ṛṣabha-prajasaha-sarva-prajñāta-cakṣur-vaktra-nikavaḥ*
Kṣatra-vaktra-kṣa-prajñā-tṛ-ni-tṛ-vyāni-tṛ-ja-sapta-kṣa-ri.
Kāruṇa-pañjarakṣaṇa, praraṇa-ṣṭhambhiya-bhiyanāruṇa-apramāṇa-pramāṇa-jaye.
Oṃ dvaya-māpata-raburaṇi sūkṣma-ra-ta-vyākṛta-yan-pi-ra-vinyana-ni-svabhāva-parā.
ānīṃ hake śiṇe śarjvalire svāhā sarajjvalire jvalitānantivāhanir jvālākasaṃtapte jvalire.
Dīpanī saka-maṇḍalokha-lekha-śakti-dhāra-prabhā-kṛṣṇa-jina-nirvṛti-accha-sūtra-dhara-vinyasa.
Ānanda-patma-kuśala-sphāra-grīṣmātara-kajvala-praṇidhāna-hanamāla-vi...
jina-prajñāraśmitrīśūriṇi-arcir-jvala jvalaya vajravetāla-paṭuma-gama-riṇi-kami.
Ṇi ṇika ma ru pi ca siddhi siddhi vara-praṇāmi-bhū-stha-laṅkṛti ni-pu-saṇa su-pu-saṇa bhūta-mātā-vi.
ŚA LA KṢI PAṆMA KI SĀRAMĀLINI PŪMINI VAJRA BHRŪÑJA VĀLOKAPRATĀNI SARVADARMA DHĀ.
raṇimai tra savyaṃ trī buddhamātā cakrandarāmini caṇi śavari śavarmūni sahasrā.
Karma mahāyogī-karma-siddha-tri-vikrama-prasanna-mukha-gaṇa-sattva-vatsala-jaya.
Gati-dhātri, pañca-nirvāṇi-supratiṣṭhita-svāhā. These one hundred and eight names are the secret mantra.
If there is one who single-mindedly upholds and recites it,
or writes it out themselves, or explains it to others,
their lifespan will increase, they will possess auspiciousness and a handsome appearance, and they will be endowed with marks of merit that all people love and revere.
They remain far removed from the realms of Māra and emerge from the hardships of birth and death;
they are venerated and offered to by devas, humans, and asuras,
and further receive the homage of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth.
The hosts of vidyādhara sages will respect and praise them;
all shackles and bonds shall be naturally released;
and [they shall be protected from] lions, tigers, wolves, and all evil hungry ghosts.
Enemies and thieves cannot oppress or harm them;
violent winds, fierce fires, clouds, rain, thunder, and hail cannot affect them;
nor can overflowing rivers and seas, poisons, or grave illnesses cause them injury or loss.
If there are those who recollect this name of Vikuṭī,
the Bodhisattva will constantly protect and guard them against all evil Māras and enemies who come to oppress and afflict them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva secretly emitted a bodily radiance that illuminated the void like hundreds of thousands of suns;
its brilliance was so intense that it utterly eclipsed and destroyed the demonic adversaries.
Even unto heaven and earth, all shall become utterly pure.
Furthermore, it shall cause that person’s wisdom to increase,
so that within seven lifetimes they attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives.
Born into the Kṣatriya caste and receiving the body of a king,
he passes away from there and is reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
*The Sūtra of the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi*.
